feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: Halloween temperatures have been trending hotter. Here's what the data shows
entry.summary: Recent analysis from research nonprofit Climate Central found that on average, fall temperatures have warmed by 2.9 degrees Fahrenheit in the U.S. and the summer heat is lasting longer.

entry.title: Here's what it's like to live in Salem, Mass., during the Halloween tourism season
entry.summary: NPR's Scott Detrow speaks with reporter Megan Johnson, who wrote about what it's like to live in Salem, Mass. — famous for the Salem Witch Trials — during Halloween tourism season.

entry.title: An experiment tested whether 100 citizens could work together to reform property taxes
entry.summary: Over the last few months, 100 randomly selected people tested whether a random bunch of citizens can work together to fix property taxes, avert a future budget crisis, and maybe reinvent democracy.

entry.title: Answering NPR listeners' questions about the good and bad of AI
entry.summary: NPR podcast Machine Gods is about the AI revolution. Hosts Kevin Roose and Casey Newton take questions from listeners about AI.

entry.title: This week in science: mysterious X-rays, movement and learning, and memory formation
entry.summary: Emily Kwong and Ari Daniel of NPR's Short Wave talk about mysterious X-ray objects, the link between movement and learning and how a small part of the brain triggers memory formation.

entry.title: How Esther Perel's parents' experience as Holocaust survivors shaped her worldview
entry.summary: Esther Perel is a famous psychotherapist and host of the podcast Where Should We Begin. She told Wild Card's Rachel Martin that her parents' experience as holocaust survivors shaped her worldview.

entry.title: How religion is influencing the midterm elections
entry.summary: Anti-Muslim rhetoric has heated up amid the Senate race in Michigan. Meanwhile, the Trump Administration promoted a meeting with Catholic bishops that some participants say left them feeling duped.

entry.title: Puerto Ricans protest record-high electricity costs
entry.summary: Billions have been invested in Puerto Rico's troubled electrical grid. Despite privatization, the blackouts continue. Protestors say they pay some of the highest electricity prices in the 50 states.

entry.title: Ebola vaccine trials begin in DRC
entry.summary: NPR's Scott Detrow speaks with Dr. Meg Doherty, director of science for health at the World Health Organization, about the clinical trials to target the Bundibugyo species of the Ebola virus.

entry.title: 'La Bola Negra' weaves literary mystery with stories of love and loss
entry.summary: Spain's official entry in the Oscar race, La Bola Negra, is a sweeping historical epic spanning nearly a century and linking stories of queer men in three eras.
